title: LoL Esports |
content:
For the first time, Tier 2 teams will come together on a global stage featuring representatives from all major LoL Esports regions.

As a collaboration between TJ Sports and Riot Games, the 2026 World Star Challengers Invitational (WSCI) will bring 16 Tier 2 teams from Asia, Europe, and the Americas together this September, giving some of the world's most promising players an opportunity to level-up the competition against opponents from outside their home regions.

WSCI is designed to open up a higher level of international competition for Tier 2 players and teams. The tournament is structured to help accelerate player development, strengthen connections between regional ecosystems, and establish a global showcase that gives fans a first look at the players who could become the next generation of LoL Esports stars.

WSCI 2026 will run fromSeptember 20-October 2. Each of the five participating regions - China, Korea, APAC, Americas, and EMEA - will utilize a mix of qualification pathways to identify 3 participating teams per region. These 15 participants will join with the Asia Masters Champion to complete the field. Teams will be placed into three seeding pools. The group draw will place one team from Pool 1, one team from Pool 2, and two teams from Pool 3 into each group. Teams from Pools 1 and 2 representing the same region cannot be drawn into the same group, and no group may contain more than two teams from any one region.

WSCI will begin with a four-group stage September 20–25. Each group will contain four teams, and every team will play every other team twice in a double round-robin format. All group-stage matches will be best-of-one for a total of 48 matches across six match days, with eight matches played each day. The top two teams from each group will advance, flowing into an eight-team championship bracket.

From September 27-October 2, the qualified teams will compete in a single-elimination bracket featuring quarterfinals, semifinals, and the final. Every bracket-stage series will be best-of-five. The bracket will consist of seven series in total and will conclude with the WSCI 2026 Final on October 2, where the tournament champion will be crowned.

summary: T1, Gen.G, Dplus in the Lol Worlds 2026 qualification: LCK playoffs stream, schedule, results  Esports.gg
content:
From the Mushroom Kingdom to Summoner’s Rift, Eugene actively explores the multidimensional world of video games and occasionally writes about his discoveries. He is fascinated by gaming competitions, believing that…

League of Legends (LoL) teams in Korea are traditionally the favorites for the Worlds trophy. In the regional playoffs, they flex their competitive muscles and battle for three qualification spots.

The long and exciting 2026 season in LoL Champions Korea (LCK) comes to an end with double-elimination playoff brackets. The top 6 teams of this strongest League of Legends esports region clash to reach the top 3 and advance to the main event of the year, LoL Worlds 2026.

All eyes are onT1players, sure. They are the reigning World Champions! To potentially extend their three-title streak, Faker and company should make it through a few highly intense rounds.

Dplusare the Esports Worlds Cup 2026 winners, and it’s interesting to check out their current state after such success.Gen.Gdominated the LCK scene in 2025 and reached the top 3 at the First Stand tournament and the EWC 2026. Not qualifying for the Mid-Season Invitational 2026 (MSI 2026) was a big disappointment for Gen.G fans

Hanwha Life Esportswon the MSI 2026 and guaranteed themselves Worlds 2026 qualification. Still, the expectations are high for them. Facing T1, Gen.G, and Dplus KIA is a nice test of true power.
